Authors: Chen Q.; Yuan A.; Kong H.; Wang K.; Wang X.; Chen K.
Title: XGBoost-SHAP-based prediction of ultimate stress increment in external tendons of prestressed concrete beams
Abstract: Accurately determining the ultimate stress increment of external tendons is difficult because external tendons are intentionally unbonded along their length, though mechanical force transfer still occurs at anchorages and deviator points. To overcome the limitations of traditional analytical methods, which rely heavily on the plane-section assumption, idealized failure mechanisms, and empirically calibrated coefficients, this work introduces a highly interpretable data-driven framework integrating the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). A comprehensive dataset of 196 physical test specimens, encompassing 19 feature variables, was assembled. The dataset is split before augmentation into 137 training specimens and 59 untouched test specimens, with feature-only Gaussian noise augmentation applied to the training set. To explore predictive robustness under incomplete geometric data, two modeling scenarios were established: one utilizing all features, and another excluding web width and flange thickness. The XGBoost model was trained with optimally tuned hyperparameters. The results indicate that the framework achieves exceptional performance, with training R² values of 0.9821 and 0.9781, and testing R² values of 0.8813 and 0.8773 for the two scenarios, respectively. SHAP analysis quantifies the marginal contributions and directional impacts of each feature, cross-validating data-driven patterns against classical mechanical principles such as deformation compatibility, Hooke’s law, and force equilibrium. Comparative assessments against traditional mechanical models and other ensemble learning methods confirm the framework’s superior accuracy, generalization, and physical interpretability. Feature importance and SHAP analyses reveal that parameters such as prestressing tendon area, compressive reinforcement area, and effective depth contribute most significantly to predictions, cumulatively accounting for over 50% of the predictive variance, and their marginal effects are highly consistent with classical structural mechanical principles. Compared to traditional models, the XGBoost framework effectively bypasses the need for predefined idealized failure mode assumptions, demonstrating clear superiority in prediction accuracy (reducing prediction errors by approximately 33% compared to the best-performing traditional analytical model) and broader applicability. When benchmarked against other ensemble learning algorithms, XGBoost exhibits the best overall performance in balancing predictive precision and resistance to overfitting. © 2026 Institution of Structural Engineers. Title: An Empirical Study of Spatial and Spectral Feature Fusion for Robust Lung Cancer Histopathology Classification Under Domain Shift and Image Perturbations
Abstract: Deep learning has demonstrated high efficiency in histopathological image analysis, particularly in lung cancer classification. However, the stability of these models with image corruption and cross-dataset validation remains an important practical concern. In this study, we explored the potential of adding spectral information derived from the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and spatial convolutional representations to enhance the robustness of multi-class lung cancer classification between Normal, Adenocarcinoma and Squamous cell carcinoma. The lightweight ResNet18 backbone was used to obtain spatial features, and spectral descriptors were obtained through wavelet sub-bands and integrated through early feature-level fusion. The models were trained and evaluated using the LC25000 dataset. Subsequently, it was tested under controlled perturbations, such as Gaussian noise and Gaussian blur. Three random seeds were used to assess performance variability, and paired t-tests were conducted as an indicative statistical measure of the results. Under clean conditions, the spatial and hybrid models were nearly saturated, and there was no significant difference between them (spatial: 99.85 ± 0.26; hybrid: 99.72 ± 0.22; p = 0.1217). The hybrid model exhibited higher robustness when Gaussian noise (σ = 0.05) was added, which resulted in 84.89% ± 4.52% accuracy versus 74.99% ± 7.20% of the spatial baseline (p = 0.0443) with an observed effect size (Cohen’s d = 2.64), noting that these estimates are based on a limited number of runs and should be interpreted with caution. The same behavior was observed in Gaussian blur perturbations, where the hybrid representation was slightly more stable. We also investigated a simplified adaptive gating mechanism process and found that the learned gate parameter also tends to converge towards spatial feature dominance with a model trained with clean data. Finally, cross-dataset validation with LungHist700 showed a slight increase in the balanced accuracy of the hybrid model (0.5158) over the spatial baseline (0.4722). These results indicate that spectral and spatial features can be used to enhance robustness to image corruption and still yield high classification accuracy, indicating that spectral–spatial representations can improve robustness under controlled perturbations, whereas their impact on cross-dataset generalization remains limited. The results further indicate that robustness improvements are strongly influenced by training strategies, such as noise augmentation, whereas the contribution of fusion is comparatively moderate. © 2026 by the authors.

Author full names: Wilkho, Rohan Singh (57201552579); Huang, Xinke (57475246500); Pitta, Venkat (60762379800); Ahmed, Afreen (60763152800); Gharaibeh, Nasir G. (6603845144)
Title: CulvertVision: Advancing AI-Augmented Inspection and Condition Assessment of Culverts
Abstract: Culvert inspection remains a persistent bottleneck in infrastructure asset management, constrained by labor-intensive manual inspection, resource limitations, and varying reporting across varied environments. This study presents CulvertVision, a deep learning framework for automated defect detection in culvert inspection videos designed to align with the Pipeline Assessment and Certification Program (PACP) standards. Utilizing a ResNet-101 architecture fine-tuned via transfer learning from sewer infrastructure benchmarks, the system processes untrimmed inspection videos to generate temporally stable classifications for four categories: corrosion, settled deposits, joint offset, and normal. Evaluation across 6,600 annotated frames under shared-video, noise-augmented, and video-disjoint configurations reveals that while noise augmentation improves robustness in controlled settings (F1-scores>0.88), a significant generalization gap emerges in out-of-distribution scenarios, with joint offset performance declining to an F1-score of 0.55. Beyond accuracy, CulvertVision's throughput analysis demonstrates high operational efficiency, offering substantial time savings compared to manual human review. By automating PACP-aligned defect detection, the framework enables agencies to streamline inspection workflows and support data-driven capital and maintenance planning. While current work explores dataset expansion through generative augmentation to address training limitations, CulvertVision represents a scalable prototype for artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented infrastructure inspection and broader field deployment.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Towards Reliable Intelligent Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Element Bearings: The Role of Signal Quality
Source title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Prognostics and Health Management, ICPHM 2026
Abstract: Reliable and interpretable fault diagnosis of rolling element bearings is essential for condition monitoring and maintenance of rotating machinery. This study investigates the impact of vibration signal quality on the performance and reliability of deep learning based fault diagnosis, using the CWRU and PU benchmark datasets under varying fault sizes. Two neural network architectures, a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and a one dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN), are evaluated using multiple input representations, including raw signals, frequency spectra, envelope spectra, and cepstrum pre-whitened envelope spectra. The results demonstrate that signal quality, particularly the presence of classical fault related features, plays a decisive role in diagnostic performance and model generalization. When high quality signals are used for training, the models achieve significantly higher accuracy and exhibit behavior consistent with classical signal analysis principles. Among the evaluated representations, envelope based features outperform other inputs in most cases, especially when combined with the 1D-CNN architecture. The effects of signal length and data augmentation are also examined. Increasing input length improves frequency resolution, while Gaussian noise augmentation during training enhances robustness, yielding accuracy improvements of up to 8.65 percent. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of signal quality awareness, informed input design, and appropriate model selection for achieving reliable fault diagnosis in realistic industrial monitoring scenarios.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: EfficientNet-B0 for Automated Bird Species Identification from Spectrogram-Encoded Vocalizations
Abstract: Automated bird species identification is essential for biodiversity monitoring and conservation, particularly for rare or elusive species where visual observation is impractical. This study presents an acoustic-based classification framework that converts bird vocalizations into spectrogram representations and applies deep transfer learning for species recognition. A dataset of 436 audio recordings from ten bird species was preprocessed through clipping, noise augmentation, pitch shifting, and time shifting to enhance model robustness. Five deep learning architectures—Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), AlexNet, VGG-19, ResNet-50, and EfficientNet-B0—were trained and evaluated on spectrogram inputs. EfficientNet-B0 consistently outperformed all other models, achieving an accuracy of 93%, precision of 94%, recall of 93%, and F1-score of 93%. The lightweight architecture and compound scaling strategy of EfficientNet-B0 enabled effective feature extraction from time-frequency representations despite the limited dataset size. To enhance practical utility, the classification output is integrated with GPT-4 Omni, which generates contextual information about the identified species, including ecological characteristics and conservation status. This integration transforms the system from a standalone classifier into a field-support tool for researchers, conservationists, and birdwatchers. The proposed framework enables non-invasive, real-time species identification using only acoustic signals, eliminating the need for visual confirmation or close proximity. This approach supports early detection, population monitoring, and biodiversity conservation while minimizing disturbance to natural bird behavior. Copyright: ©2026 The authors. Authors: Wang Y.; Hu L.; Xue Z.; Li Q.; Li J.; Kong X.
Title: Training-only ultrasound-specific augmentation for ovarian tumor segmentation across B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound
Abstract: Background – Ovarian tumor segmentation models trained on conventional ultrasound may be sensitive to contrast-enhanced ultrasound appearance. We evaluated whether training-only combined ultrasound-specific augmentation could improve robustness without adding inference-time complexity. Methods – We used MMOTU image-mask pairs, including 820 development B-mode ultrasound images, 382 internal two-dimensional ultrasound images, and 170 contrast-enhanced ultrasound images as a CEUS domain-shift stress test. A lightweight Residual U-Net was compared with the same backbone trained using photometric, blur, and low-amplitude noise augmentation. Performance was evaluated using overlap, boundary, and pixel-calibration metrics. Paired CEUS differences were tested with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and effect sizes, 95% confidence intervals, and case-level failure rates were reported. Results – The combined augmentation preserved internal performance, with Dice of 0.745 (0.196) compared with 0.750 (0.191) for Residual U-Net. On contrast-enhanced ultrasound, it improved Dice from 0.468 (0.190) to 0.476 (0.192), intersection over union from 0.326 (0.167) to 0.334 (0.171), Boundary F1 from 0.037 (0.035) to 0.041 (0.032), and pixel expected calibration error from 0.314 (0.143) to 0.297 (0.138). The mean paired CEUS Dice improvement was 0.008 (95% CI -0.0002 to 0.0167); 62.9% of cases improved and 37.1% worsened. However, the proportion of CEUS cases with Dice below 0.5 decreased from 55.9 to 51.8%, indicating that CEUS segmentation remained suboptimal. Conclusion – Training-only combined ultrasound-specific augmentation yielded a small but directionally favorable CEUS improvement without added inference-time complexity. These findings support training-distribution design as a practical low-cost strategy for modality-shift robustness and warrant further patient-level and multi-center validation. Title: Generative tabular data augmentation for sensorless metallic foreign object localization in wireless power transfer systems
Abstract: As wireless power transfer (WPT) for electric vehicles (EVs) accelerates towards commercialization, the inadvertent presence of metallic foreign objects (MFOs) in the magnetic coupling region poses severe safety hazards and degrades transfer efficiency. While traditional hardware-based detection methods increase system complexity and cost, sensorless data-driven approaches are heavily constrained by the scarcity and extreme class imbalance of experimental data (up to a 16:1 ratio). To explicitly overcome this bottleneck, this study proposes a sensorless multi-class MFO localization framework that synergizes physics-informed electrical features derived from load and efficiency measurements with advanced tabular data augmentation. Utilizing a custom-built 140 W WPT platform, experimental data were systematically acquired across 11 distinct spatial grid positions. Six generative models were benchmarked alongside conventional SMOTE and Gaussian-noise augmentation using CatBoost and LightGBM classifiers under a bounded class-aware augmentation strategy. On the fixed held-out test set, CopulaGAN achieved the highest observed accuracy of 80.82%. Additional five-fold out-of-fold validation over all 1456 measured samples showed significant CopulaGAN accuracy gains over no-augmentation training for both CatBoost and LightGBM, supporting the robustness of the observed gains within the present dataset. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Learning across modalities: Multi-scale contrastive forecasting with time-frequency representations and adversarial augmentations
Abstract: Time series forecasting is crucial across diverse fields, yet existing deep learning models struggle with multi-scale dependencies, noise robustness, and cross-domain feature alignment. This paper introduces MFF-FTNet, a novel multi-modal forecasting framework that leverages contrastive learning across time and frequency representations, reinforced by adversarial augmentations. MFF-FTNet incorporates an adaptive noise augmentation strategy, which dynamically perturbs input sequences based on statistical properties, improving robustness against noise and distribution shifts. The architecture integrates two key components: Multi-Modal Frequency Contrastive Learning (MM-FCL), which refines spectral representations through adaptive frequency selection and contrastive alignment, and Multi-Modal Temporal Hypergraph Contrastive Learning (MM-TCL), which models high-order dependencies using multi-scale convolutions and hypergraph-based feature fusion. By unifying these perspectives within a cross-modal contrastive learning framework, MFF-FTNet effectively aligns time-frequency representations, enhancing forecasting accuracy across varying conditions. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that MFF-FTNet achieves a 7.7% MSE improvement on multivariate forecasting tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art models. These results highlight the model's ability to capture complex temporal structures, handle sparsity, and improve generalization, making it a robust solution for both short-term and long-term forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Pre-trained under Noise: A Framework for Robust Bone Fracture Detection in Medical Imaging
Source title: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence, ICMI 2026
Abstract: Medical Imagings are considered one of the crucial diagnostic tools for different bones-related diseases, especially bones fractures. This paper investigates the robustness of pre-trained deep learning models for classifying bone fractures in X-ray images and seeks to address global healthcare disparity through the lens of technology. Three deep learning models have been tested under varying simulated equipment quality conditions. ResNet50, VGG16 and EfficientNetv2 are the three pre-trained architectures which are compared. These models were used to perform bone fracture classification as images were progressively degraded using noise. This paper specifically empirically studies how the noise can affect the bone fractures detection and how the pre-trained models performance can be changes due to the noise that affect the quality of the X-ray images. This paper aims to help replicate real world challenges experienced by medical imaging technicians across the world. Thus, this paper establishes a methodological framework for assessing AI model degradation using transfer learning and controlled noise augmentation. The findings provide practical insight into how robust and generalizable different pre-trained deep learning powered computer vision models can be when used in different contexts. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Yang Y.; Wang J.; Li Y.; An W.; Cai J.
Title: A mechanism-data dual-driven approach for predicting profile changes in rails
Abstract: Accurate prediction of rail profile changes is crucial for scientifically formulating rail wear mitigation strategies, maintaining track reliability, and ensuring economic benefit. However, traditional models based on rail wear mechanisms are limited in prediction accuracy due to their idealized assumptions. While possessing strong nonlinear fitting capabilities, data-driven models often lack interpretability and rely on large amounts of high-quality training data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel method that integrates the advantages of both approaches to predict rail profile changes. Utilizing a prototype network, a rail profile change model is pre-trained with simulation data and then fine-tuned using measurement rail profile data through transfer learning. K-fold cross-validation and noise augmentation are employed to enhance the model's prediction accuracy and robustness. The study results indicate that for tracks with curve radii between 400 and 600 m, the precision of 10 random prediction trials exceeds 90 %, with standard deviations of Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) being 0.03397 mm2, 0.04261 mm, 0.0204 mm, and 0.175 %, respectively, demonstrating excellent predictive accuracy and stability. Compared to models using only measurement data, this method achieves reductions in average MSE, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by 30.60 %, 11.76 %, 12.94 %, and 10.45 %, respectively. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.
